name: amcache_apps
description: Application and file inventory from Amcache.hve (presence, not execution): path, hash, publisher, version and the dates the inventory holds, from both the older Root\File layout (numbered values, named by the published mapping regipy's Amcache plugin follows) and the newer InventoryApplicationFile layout (named values), read together, every row naming its layout. An inventory: an entry is not proof that a program ran, and the absence of one is not proof that it did not. The PE linker timestamp (value f) is a 32-bit Unix-epoch value and is converted as one (raw value kept); the key's last-written time and the 11, 12 and 17 values are FILETIMEs (raw decimal and ISO 8601 UTC with seven fractional digits). A hash is returned as stored (sha1_raw) with its stripped form beside it where it has the four-zero shape; what range of the file was hashed is not established. It reports hive_dirty from the base block's sequence numbers and the transaction logs beside the hive; it replays none. Every list of subkeys and values is read through the size of the hive: a hive of N bytes holds at most N/76 keys and N/20 values, so an index that repeats one list (an ri element named again and again) is read to that bound, listed once per key, and said under problems; it is not followed. A value whose name is one of the tool's own fields (layout, key, volume, sha1_raw...) is kept as value:<name>, never over the field. Problems are a page (the first 40 inline, all in all_problems). The tool stops at its own time limit (85 seconds) and says partial; SIGTERM, SIGINT and SIGHUP end it with JSON and no temporary file; a result file is never replaced. The library's own messages are counted and never printed. status is complete or partial (problems, a time stop) and status_basis says which. WITHHOLDING (one boundary on every way out). Every key and value of the answer, and every row of every file this tool writes, is judged by the type of the field it fills (paths, names, publishers and hashes): a name, path, key or URL is shown as it is only when it fits a plain grammar (a path component by component; GUIDs, SIDs, addresses, 0x numbers, times and hexadecimal ids up to 24 digits are plain), free text has token-shaped runs, user-info, the value after a secret's name, vendor-prefixed tokens, padded base64 and PEM keys withheld, and a second check written apart from the first reads it all once more, the text as the evidence wrote it as well as the text shown (a piece of 12 characters of a secret that two cuts left behind is caught) (a string it replaces makes a complete answer partial and is listed under boundary.replaced_at, by the keys on the way as they are shown or by positions, never by a withheld key). A withheld text is <withheld N characters: reason>. Binary data written as hexadecimal is decoded and judged by its printable text, by both layers and by the backstop on its own; hexadecimal with no secret-shaped text in it is shown as it is, random bytes included (a binary key is printed). write_values: true writes the originals of everything withheld to <tool>-values.jsonl (mode 0600, created first, never replaced) and is accepted only in a job the harness runs as secret output (the manifest declares it; SECRET_OUTPUT=1), refused as JSON anywhere else before anything is made. Measured on random plants of every shape in 13 slots (988 per shape; the tests plant them again): prefixed tokens (GitHub, GitLab, Stripe, SendGrid, Google, npm, AWS key ids), JWT, PEM keys (one line and several), connection strings, user-info (an @, a / or a + inside the password, a random user of any length, a GitLab token glued to hexadecimal digits), NUL, zero-width and full-width splits, upper-case and glued prefixes, AWS-shaped secret keys of 40 characters: none printed whole and no piece of 12 characters of one printed; 16, 20 and 32-byte base64 keys: at most 0.1% overall (worst slot 1.3%); random base62 of 20 to 40 characters: at most 0.4% overall (worst slot 2.6%); random lower-case letters of 24: 8.5% overall, 16% in the worst slot; a 16-character base32 seed: 11% overall, 18% in the worst slot. In a binary slot (a hexadecimal REG_BINARY value or table cell) the backstop decodes the hexadecimal and replaces every hex-encoded shape it claims (480 of 480 plants), but random bytes that hold no text are printed (200 of 200), and so is a hexadecimal secret written as text there (a 32-digit one in a table cell: 97%). Real Windows strings changed (any part withheld) in 9,950 generated registry, file, service, package and host names, SIDs, GUIDs and typed digests (2 changed: the 32-digit hash in a Chrome and an Edge autolaunch value name) and 3,431 strings of real event logs (25 changed: 17 of 1,040 whole event records, 7 of 313 command lines and messages, 1 of 322 path fields; they hold encoded PowerShell payloads and the 32-digit hash directories of the .NET native-image cache). Strings the shape rules change that are not secrets: numbers of 19 digits or more (handles, a Chrome field-trial handle, a mojo pipe name), unlabelled hexadecimal runs of 32 digits or more (the native-image directories), and the query values of a URL in a URL slot. NOT recognised, by design: a secret that does not look like one (a plain password or passphrase, a pronounceable passphrase, a UUID-shaped key, a hexadecimal secret of up to 24 digits in a name or of any length in a binary slot, anything under 16 characters in a name; 75% to 100% of such plants are printed): withholding is by shape, so a file whose secrets matter is read in a job run with secret_output: true.

limit.description: Entries shown inline (default 500, an inline page size); every entry is kept, and when there are more the whole list is written as JSON Lines and named in all_results

write_values.description: Write the originals of everything the boundary withheld to a file under $OUT (mode 0600, created first, never replaced): only in a job run with secret_output: true, refused anywhere else; default false
